editorial.marketOverview: The last completed U.S. cash session ended in a broad selloff: Nasdaq -2.25%, S&P 500 -2.02%, more than 90% decliners and VIX 28.44. A same-source secondary report places QQQ -2.19% versus SPY -1.97%. The failed IPO-led relief rally and weak chip leadership support continued caution for November 20, 23 and 24.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the 19:50 EST assessment, additional secondary QQQ/SPY closing figures show 0.22 percentage points of QQQ underperformance. WSJ reports WTI December $83.21 and Brent January $91.98 at settlement. These refine evidence but do not constitute a material outlook change. Curated Open Watch remains at 171 unchanged events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Broad distribution and volatility expansion outweigh selective IPO strength. Six consecutive S&P declines raise the chance of a technical rebound, not proof of a durable turn. Treasury yield curve observations are stale and oil futures are different contract months, limiting cross-market inference. No new market response to Friday events has occurred.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20 is the immediate test of whether a recovery can sustain after Thursday's reversal. Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations at 10:00 EST are scheduled, not yet observed. Continued semiconductor underperformance and weak breadth would favor downside continuation Monday November 23 and Tuesday November 24. Broad QQQ/SOX recovery and lower volatility would challenge that path.
editorial.bullCase: Oversold conditions and Anthropic holding above IPO price allow a relief bounce. To confirm durable upside require QQQ relative strength, SOX/SMH leadership, improving breadth and falling VXN/VIX with stable or lower yields. Those conditions have not been established.
editorial.bearCase: The failed rally, Nasdaq -2.25%, >90% decliners, VIX 28.44 and Nvidia -3.3% establish elevated downside risk. Friday's failed rebound could carry weakness into Monday and Tuesday. Company-specific after-hours earnings disappointment is a potential sentiment headwind, not proof of index-wide reaction.
